sentences.text: Today we will talk about Venice.
Venice is a city in Italy.
It is one of the most famous and beautiful cities in the world.
Venice is special because it is built on water.
There are no cars in the city.
People travel by boats.
The city has many small islands connected by bridges.
The blue water, old houses and narrow streets make Venice look like a dream.
Many people visit Venice every year to see its beauty, history and art.
Let's learn more about this wonderful city together.
Part two, history of Venice.
Venice has a very long and interesting history.
The city was founded more than 1,500 years ago.
People built their homes on small islands to stay safe from enemies.
Over time, Venice became a rich and powerful city because of trade.
Ships came from many countries to buy and sell goods.
For many years, Venice was known as La Serenissima, which means the most peaceful.
It was one of the most important cities in Europe.
Today, Venice is famous for its history and culture.
The old buildings tell stories of a great past.
Part three, famous people from Venice.
Many famous people were born in Venice.
One of them is Marco Polo, a great explorer who traveled from Venice to China hundreds of years ago.
Another famous person is Antonio Vivaldi, a composer who wrote beautiful music.
His most famous work is the Four Seasons.
Venice is also home to many painters, writers and artists who made the city known around the world.
Even today, Venice inspires many creative people.
Art and beauty are part of everyday life here.
Part four, the canals of Venice.
Venice is built on water and canals are like its streets.
There are more than 150 canals in the city.
The biggest one is the Grand Canal.
It goes through the center of Venice and is full of boats and gondolas.
A gondola is a long black boat that moves gently on the water.
Gondola rides are very popular among tourists.
You can see old buildings and bridges while you ride.
The sound of the water is calm and peaceful.
The canals make Venice unique.
There is no other city like it in the world.
Part five, famous buildings and places.
Venice has many beautiful buildings.
One of the most famous is St.
Mark's Basilica, a big church with golden domes and colorful mosaics.
Next to it is St.
Mark's Square, the main square of Venice.
It is full of people, music and pigeons.
Another important place is the Doge's Palace, where old leaders of Venice lived.
It has tall arches, art and marble walls.
Don't forget the Rialto Bridge, one of the oldest bridges across the Grand Canal.
It is a perfect place to take photos.
Every building in Venice tells a story.
Part six, food in Venice.
Food in Venice is delicious.
Because the city is near the sea, people eat a lot of fish.
One popular dish is risotto al narrow di seppia, rice cooked with black squid ink.
It looks dark, but tastes wonderful.
Another is sardine and sour, made with sardines, onions and vinegar.
Venice is also famous for small snacks called chicchetti.
You can eat them in local bars called Bacari.
And of course, Italian ice cream, gelato is everywhere.
Eating gelato while walking near the canals is a sweet memory.
Part seven, the people of Venice.
People in Venice are friendly and proud of their city.
Many families have lived there for generations.
Life in Venice is different because of the water.
People use boats to go to school, work or shop.
Venetians love their traditions, music and festivals.
They enjoy simple things, walking by the water, drinking coffee and talking with friends.
They also care a lot about their city and want to protect it from floods and pollution.
Venetians are warm, artistic and full of life.
Part eight, art and culture.
Venice is full of art and culture.
There are museums, theaters and galleries everywhere.
The Venice Biennale is a big art event that happens every two years.
Artists from all over the world come to show their work.
The city is also known for its beautiful Murano glass.
It is made by hand on a nearby island.
You can find colorful glass faces, jewelry and decorations.
Venice has music, painting and architecture that show its great love for beauty.
Art is in the soul of Venice.
Part nine, festivals in Venice.
One of the most famous festivals in the world happens in Venice, the Carnival of Venice.
During Carnival, people wear beautiful masks and costumes.
There are music, dancing and parades everywhere.
The masks are colorful and full of gold, feathers and jewels.
Another big event is the Venice Film Festival where many famous actors and directors come to show new movies.
Festivals in Venice are full of color, joy and excitement.
The city becomes even more magical.
Part ten, islands near Venice.
Venice is made of many islands and some of them are very special.
Murano is famous for glass making.
You can see how artists create glass with fire.
Murano is another island known for its colorful houses and handmade lace.
Every house has a different bright color, pink, blue, yellow or green.
Torcello is quiet and peaceful with old churches in nature.
Each island has its own charm.
Visiting them shows the many sides of Venice.
Part eleven, tourism and travel.
Many people visit Venice every year.
It is one of the top travel places in the world.
Tourists walk through narrow streets, ride gondolas and take photos on bridges.
Hotels and cafes are everywhere and people enjoy coffee or pasta by the water.
Traveling in Venice can be a little tricky because of the canals but it's also exciting and fun.
Even when it rains the city looks like a painting.
Venice is a place you will never forget.
Part twelve, goodbye from Venice.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
Venice is a city like no other.
It has water instead of streets, boats instead of cars and music in the air.
You can see art, history and beauty everywhere you look.
The people, food and festivals make it full of life.
I hope you can visit Venice one day.
You will fall in love with its charm and magic.
